text: What is a telerally? Trump's tele-rallies before the midterms. A telerally is a rally held by phone or video rather than in person, in which a political figure speaks to supporters and voters from a distance. Before the Nov. 3, 2026 midterm elections, the Republican National Committee planned Trump telerallies aimed at nearly 20 states.. The word spread after the RNC swapped two of Trump's final midterm rallies for telerallies on Oct. 29, 2026. The in-person rallies were restored a day later and held on Nov. 1.. A telerally (also written tele-rally, plural telerallies) lets one speaker reach voters in many states at once, with no travel, crowd or venue. Supporters listen in by phone or online instead of standing in an arena. Trump had used the format before. In late October 2025 he spoke at a telerally for Jack Ciattarelli, the Republican candidate for governor of New Jersey, and on Nov. 3, 2025 he held one for Winsome Earle-Sears in Virginia. On Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, the RNC said it would replace planned in-person stops in Iowa and Kansas with a "72-hour sprint" of telerallies across nearly 20 states, including Michigan, Alaska, Texas and Iowa. Party chairman Joe Gruters argued that virtual events reach more voters than single stops. Asked why he was skipping Kansas, Trump said, "I don't feel I have to go to Kansas." The plan changed a day later. On Oct. 30 the Iowa and Kansas rallies were put back on the schedule, and on Sunday, Nov. 1, Trump spoke in person in Dubuque, Iowa, and Salina, Kansas, two days before the vote.

When is Cyber Monday 2026? Nov. 30, the Monday after Thanksgiving. Cyber Monday 2026 falls on Monday, November 30. It is the Monday after Thanksgiving (Nov. 26) and three days after Black Friday (Nov. 27). Retailers use it for online-only discounts, and in recent years it has been the biggest online shopping day of the year in the U.S.. With Black Friday on Nov. 27, 2026, retailers have already started early holiday sales, and shoppers are checking the Cyber Monday date.. The name was coined in 2005 by Shop.org, part of the National Retail Federation, after retailers noticed a jump in online orders on the Monday after Thanksgiving. Because it follows Thanksgiving, the date moves each year and always falls between Nov. 26 and Dec. 2. In 2027 it will be Nov. 29. Cyber Monday 2025 (Dec. 1, 2025) set a record of $14.25 billion in U.S. Online spending, according to Adobe Analytics, making it the biggest online shopping day ever. For the 2026 season, Adobe forecast $275.1 billion in U.S. Online sales from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31. Many deals now start well before the day itself. Walmart announced three holiday sales events running from Nov. 12 through Dec. 2, 2026, and Target scheduled an early Black Friday sale for Nov. 5–7, 2026. Many stores keep Cyber Monday prices going for the rest of that week, often called Cyber Week.

What are oil prices now? Brent at $98.29 a barrel on Nov. 5, 2026. Oil prices are the per-barrel cost of crude oil, quoted through benchmark futures contracts such as Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI). On Nov. 5, 2026, Brent settled at $98.29 a barrel, up $3.67, while WTI closed at $90.52. The figures move daily as traders react to the Iran war and shipping attacks in the Gulf.. Brent crude rose more than $3 on Nov. 5, 2026, after new tanker attacks in the Gulf, reversing a sharp fall the day before. Oil has swung widely since the US, Israel and Iran went to war in February, and fuel costs became a major issue in the midterm elections.. Brent rose 3.88% on Thursday, Nov. 5, after new strikes on tankers raised concern about supply. The day before, both benchmarks had fallen more than 8%, reaching their lowest closing levels since Aug. 31. Analysts described the rebound as caution that shipping would not return to normal quickly, even if diplomacy advanced. Attacks on tankers in the Gulf are running close to a record pace. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency counted at least five vessels reporting incidents since Sunday, Nov. 1. October saw 35 vessels hit, the highest monthly total of the conflict. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents after attempting to use unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Forecasts differ sharply. Rapidan Energy's Bob McNally put the chance of renewed US military action at 80% and expects both benchmarks to top $100. Eurasia Group, by contrast, lowered its odds of renewed US strikes to 60% and its odds of a deal to 10%. Iran has reportedly proposed a nuclear deal through Qatar, but only after Washington meets what Tehran calls "seven demands," including ending the naval blockade of Iranian ports.
